roles.summary: Lead product for CLMS and SwiftChat, from a 13-section PRD to an **89% engagement lift** across **15M+ students**.
bullets: **CLMS (Jul 2025-Present):** Lead CLMS, ConveGenius's content and learning management platform, unifying content creation, translation, and distribution across client instances, including government education partners
Defined a role-based access model across five user types (Super Admin, Admin, Creator, Reviewer, Translator), enforcing a strict content-approval hierarchy from creation to publish
Drove requirements for multilingual translation and localization workflows, enabling content distribution to downstream client systems via API, CSV, and JSON exports
Took **Assessment Creation** from an unvalidated prototype to a production-ready feature, writing a 13-section PRD covering UX, edge cases, and acceptance criteria
At launch, achieved **80% flow-completion rate**, sub-3-minute Quick Generate path, sub-8-minute manual build path, and zero support tickets requiring engineering intervention
Reduced assessment creation time from hours to **under 5 minutes** for teachers, non-technical content managers, and curriculum leads
**SwiftChat (Apr 2024-Jun 2025):** Promoted from Product Associate to lead vision and roadmap for SwiftChat, ConveGenius's AI chatbot platform for education, reaching **15M+ students** nationwide
Improved engagement on SwiftChat by **89%** through iterative A/B testing, feature experimentation, and personalization
Partnered with design and engineering to turn user insights into shipped features across SwiftChat's chatbot experience
Collaborated with content and partnerships teams to launch scalable learning products for diverse student audiences

roles.summary: Shipped **25+ SwiftChat bots**, including the platform's first 3D-integrated bot, driving up to **89% year-over-year engagement gains**.
bullets: Delivered **25+ learning and engagement products** on SwiftChat, from concept to launch
Redesigned onboarding and conversation flows, reducing user drop-offs and improving retention
Developed two Python utilities: an image-to-text converter and a real-time API uptime checker that caught third-party failures before they caused outages
Personally coded the **first SwiftChat bot with 3D model integration** (Periodic Table Bot) using AI-assisted development, taking engineering load off the tech team
Drove **31-89% year-over-year engagement gains** across five engagement bots by shipping persistent menus, cross-bot discovery, and scorecards

projectsSection.subhead: Alongside that, four self-directed products I shipped solo, live and clickable:

recognition.title: VARMS · Visitor & Resource Management System
recognition.text: Built for the 330 Field Regiment, Indian Army. I volunteered to lead a remote team through a two-weekend sprint to conceive, build, and deploy a database system for the regiment's administrative and HRMS workflows.
recognition.quote: I take this opportunity to convey my profound appreciation for the outstanding work by you in designing and development of database digitization and management software VARMS for the unit.
recognition.quoteAttribution: Letter of Appreciation, Commanding Officer Col Ankit Misra, Jan 2026
why: Replaced a large stack of non-digital records that took hours to cross-check for basic answers.
Spent nearly 40% of the two-weekend sprint understanding the problem before writing any code, even under a hard deadline.
In daily use at the unit since deployment, without issues.
recognition.note: A private deployment for the Indian Army; there's no public link to visit.

projects.screenshotAlt: Yanks TCG live sale homepage showing stock counts and category cards
projects.title: Yanks TCG · Live Sale Platform
projects.description: A real-time marketplace for a Pokémon card collector's WhatsApp community, with live bidding and numbered "Box Break" claims.
why: Sellers were running inventory and sales entirely over WhatsApp DMs — needed real browsing without losing the WhatsApp relationship.
Bid instead of fixed price: low-stock, high-demand cards were going unsold at a fixed price. Bidding matches scarcity to buyer FOMO and moves them.
Numbered Box Break slots turn pack-opening into a live event — buyers pick a "lucky number" for the card behind it.
Bidding ended up the most-used feature: cards that sat unsold for months started moving once listed as bids.

projects.screenshotAlt: Yanks Diecast live sale homepage with filters and stock counts
projects.title: Yanks Diecast · Live Sale Platform
projects.description: The same marketplace engine, extended for diecast car collectors with faceted search and dynamic pricing across dozens of live SKUs.
why: Validated with a poll in the WhatsApp community first — over 70% wanted a diecast line before I built it.

projects.screenshotAlt: Math Tug-of-War game screen with team selection and difficulty levels
projects.title: Math Tug-of-War · Classroom Game
projects.description: A tug-of-war math game for classroom touchscreen TVs, with five difficulty tiers and a streak-based "Fire Mode."
why: Built for two teams to compete head-to-head on a shared classroom touchscreen, turning solo math practice into something social.
Streak-based Fire Mode rewards speed and accuracy under time pressure, not just correct answers.

projects.screenshotAlt: Krishna Kunj Stays room selection screen for ordering food
projects.title: Krishna Kunj Stays · Room Service
projects.description: A room-service ordering tool built for the homestay I lived at, after one too many phone calls and WhatsApp messages to the owner just to order food. Guests pick their room, browse the menu, and the order gets formatted and sent straight to the kitchen over WhatsApp.
why: Built after typing out the same WhatsApp message one too many times just to order coffee during a stay — wanted to cut that friction on both sides.
Deliberately skipped payments and accounts: the goal was saving time, not building a transaction platform.
Adopted for day-to-day use at the homestay.
